1.he: וְיָצַקְתִּי מַיִם עַל יְדֵי חֲכָמִים מְחֻכָּמִים
1.note: 2 Kgs 3:11: Elisha "poured water on the hands of Elijah", that is, he served him as a disciple. "Wisest of the wise" renders חכמים מחכמים (Prov 30:24).

2.note: Deut 9:21 (compare Exod 32:20) is said of the golden calf, which Moses ground to dust. The quack uses it of his eye powder.

3.note: In medieval humoral medicine a "cold" temperament in a woman was a cause of barrenness; warming remedies were given for it.

4.note: The same word twice: מָזוֹר is "cure" (Jer 30:13) and also "sore, wound" (Hos 5:13). The pun cannot be kept in English.

5.note: 2 Sam 18:3, where David's men ask him to stay in the city and send them help from there. Here the sense is only "I will be your helper".

6.note: Dan 8:4, the ram in Daniel's vision goring west and north. The healed cripple leaps like a hart (Isa 35:6) and then charges like Daniel's ram: a comic overstatement.

7.note: Literally "every eye overturned". Possibly a turned-out eyelid or a squint; the exact ailment is uncertain. The rhyme פּוּךְ / שָׁפוּךְ / הָפוּךְ carries the line.

8.note: Prov 7:9 "in the blackness (אִישׁוֹן) of night". אִישׁוֹן is also "pupil of the eye", the word in the line before; the pun is the point of the couplet.

9.he: אוֹ תְבַלּוּל בְּעֵינוֹ. אוֹ גָרָב אוֹ יַלֶּפֶת
9.note: Lev 21:20, the bodily blemishes that bar a priest from service. The exact ailments are uncertain: תְּבַלּוּל is a spot or film in the eye; גָּרָב and יַלֶּפֶת are scaly or itching skin diseases.

10.note: נִכְפֶּה is the rabbinic term for an epileptic (literally "one who is overpowered"). The lines before (falling, choking, slavering) also describe a fit.

11.note: In the Bible (Deut 28:22, 1 Kgs 8:37) these are diseases of grain, mildew and blight. In rabbinic Hebrew יֵרָקוֹן is also jaundice in a person; שִׁדָּפוֹן has no human sense, which may be part of the joke.

12.he: וּכְלֵי הַשֶּׁתֶן בָּאִים עַל כַּמָּה מִינִים. וְכֵלִים מִכֵּלִים שׁוֹנִים
12.note: Uroscopy: patients brought flasks of urine for the physician to judge by colour. "Vessels of diverse vessels" is from Esth 1:7, the wine vessels at Ahasuerus' feast.
